chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: The Berry Brothers as the greatest act he saw
summary: Crawford calls the Berry Brothers the greatest act he ever saw and describes their flips and struts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Greatest show -- greatest act I ever saw -- I think it was in Buffalo. Now, (inaudible) --
Now, you say -- what did you say? The greatest act you ever saw was what?
What was it that they did that made them your favorite?

Oh, the flips and struts, flips and strips, (inaudible) Berry big mouth, singing "Sweet Papadee," da-da-dee-da-da-dadoo-dee. --(inaudible) -- Arnis Berry every time he says Sweet Papa dee, zump, da, zump, off Raymond Berry's arm, and he's hitting that hat down there with it, tall hat.
Then Berry Brothers, sweet -- Pete Peaches and Duke, great act, sharp. And, lord, I could name so many.
But the Berry Brothers was your favorite?
